title: Contract Management for Non-Contract Professionals
overview: The primary objective of this course is to equip participants with the knowledge, skills, and tools needed to manage and administer contracts effectively after they are awarded. Through this interactive program, participants will gain insight into the processes and activities essential for fulfilling contractual obligations. The course also focuses on best practices for contract administration to ensure smooth implementation.
audience: This course is ideal for professionals involved in implementing, managing, or administering contracts. It is also beneficial for those involved in contract preparation and award phases who want to understand the importance of comprehensive contract management.
methodology: This course uses individual and group exercises to familiarize participants with practical tools and techniques for contract implementation. Case studies and role-playing activities are incorporated to enhance understanding, followed by group discussions to reinforce learning.
objectivesIntro: By the end of the course, participants will be able to:
objectives: Identify the critical steps in contract preparation, including creating an effective scope of work.
Outline key activities and stages in contract administration.
Utilize tools and techniques for effective contract implementation and understand the role of a contract administrator.
Develop systems to evaluate contractors and assess their performance.
Explain various types of variation orders, claims, and damages, and their implications.

items.text: Common challenges in contract preparation and management
Overview of contracting methods: bidding and negotiation
Drafting an effective scope of work
Consequences of poorly defined scopes of work
Roles and responsibilities in contract administration
Developing schedule and risk management plans
Addressing money damages and equitable remedies
Exploring alternative dispute resolution methods: mediation and arbitration
